bullets.title: Roadrunner: A Film About Anthony Bourdain
bullets.note: from Academy Award-winning filmmaker [Morgan Neville](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Morgan_Neville). I deeply appreciated the nuanced portrayal. The archival and outtake footage alone made it well worth watching. The official description: “_Roadrunner: A Film About Anthony Bourdain_ is an intimate, behind-the-scenes look at how an anonymous chef who lived his life unabashedly became a world-renowned cultural icon.” [Find the trailer here](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ihEEjwRlghQ). There are certainly lessons to be learned from the light and the dark, and this film raises important questions for me. For example: How can you emulate certain characteristics of tortured outliers without inadvertently absorbing beliefs and behaviors that contributed to their pain? Is it even possible? Tony’s story is inspiring, incredible, and tragic, and this film does an admirable job of capturing all three.
